passage:
A black-and-white photo showed people standing in waist-deep water on a city street. Students first thought it was from another country.
Then they learned the street was near their school.
The teacher asked them to compare the photo with modern flood maps. Some risky areas remained the same, even though buildings had changed.
The photo made climate and planning feel local.
Students wrote letters to the city asking how flood risk was being managed today.
The old photo was not just a memory of past disaster. It was evidence that water remembers low places, even when people build new roads over them.
